incbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 3901234567 - eu-central-1 inference cluster — elevated GPU driver resets and ECC corrected spikes detected. Auto-paging oncall. Severity: P1.

jen (oncall): Acknowledged. Looking now. Which pools/nodes are affected?

maria (sre): Seeing a cluster-level spike in Xid 43 and Xid 31 across nodes: inf-node-12, inf-node-18, inf-node-22. NVidia driver resets, containers restarting.

kai (eng-runtime): Logs show repeated `nvidia: GPU has fallen off the bus` followed by `Xid 43` around same timestamps. Also KVCACHE OOM on a few containers before driver reset. Snippet:```
Apr 12 03:11:42 inf-node-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 43
Apr 12 03:11:42 inf-node-12 dockerd[...]: container runtime: kill -9 (OOM)
```

jen (oncall): Current customer impact? Any 5xx spikes or errors surfaced?

tom (support): Customer-facing dashboards show a small spike in 503s for the embed API between 03:11-03:15 in eu-central. A handful of sessions retried. No long-lived data loss. Key customers A and B reported degraded latency.

raj (customer-ops): I'm drafting a short status for impacted customers: noting transient errors, we're mitigating with routing to fallback dedicated capacity. Will share in 10.

maria (sre): Immediate mitigation steps proposed: cordon + drain inf-node-12 and inf-node-18, set node selectors to avoid inf-node-* series during canary. Also bump capacity for dedicated pool eu-dedicated-1.

kai (eng-runtime): Agreed. Also will disable prefix caching on affected model routes temporarily — KVCACHE OOM might be a contributing factor. Command to disable: `PUT /routes/{r}/config {"cache":false}`.

jen (oncall): Proceeding to cordon inf-node-12 and drain. Running `kubectl cordon inf-node-12 && kubectl drain inf-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.

ops-bot: Evacuation job started for inf-node-12. Pod count: 24 -> 0. Estimated time: ~2m/pod.

maria (sre): While drain is progressing, capture full nvidia-smi -q and dmesg dumps and upload to incident artifacts. Commands:```
sudo nvidia-smi -q > /var/tmp/nvidia-q.log
sudo dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 > /var/tmp/dmesg-tail.log
journalctl -u docker -n 200 > /var/tmp/docker-journ.log
```

kai (eng-runtime): I'll pull the dumps after drain completes. Also enabling verbose driver logging on the canary nodes to capture any parity/ECC faults details.

jen (oncall): inf-node-12 drained successfully. Cordon persisted. Moving to inf-node-18 now.

ops-bot: inf-node-12 drain complete. Pods rescheduled to other nodes. No immediate crashloops observed.

tom (support): Early telemetry: 503 spike subsided after routing away from the two nodes. Still seeing occasional retries from one large customer.

maria (sre): Note — inf-node-22 shows lower-level parity reversals (correctable ECC), not only Xid. Could be a hardware degradation pattern. Proposing quarantine of inf-node-22 for further hardware checks if Xid continues.

kai (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: kernel-level GPU driver resets triggered by a combination of KVCACHE memory pressure in certain model runtimes + underlying card corrected-ECC flares causing retries. We'll prioritize reproducing with a load test that stresses KVCACHE and long sequences.

jen (oncall): Temporary workaround checklist executed: cordon/drain effected, routing to dedicated pools, cache disabled on affected routes, driver verbose logging enabled. Anything else for immediate?

maria (sre): Please schedule in a maintenance window to reboot inf-node-18 once drain completes and perform full hardware diagnostics with vendor. If we see further Xid 43 on other nodes, escalate to replacement.

raj (customer-ops): Customer status update drafted and posted to affected customers. Language: brief, apologetic, mitigation steps, ETA for next update 30m.

kai (eng-runtime): Captured logs show KVCACHE eviction thrashing before a few crashes. Example line: `kvcache: allocate failed, size=128MB, available=2MB`. That aligns with OOM before driver reset. I'll push a config tweak to reduce initial KVCACHE reservation on 3 node pools.

jen (oncall): inf-node-18 drained and cordoned. Reboot scheduled now.

ops-bot: Reboot of inf-node-18 initiated.

maria (sre): After reboot, run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and capture vendor diagnostics. Marking node for vendor RMA if parity/ECC corrected rates remain elevated.

tom (support): Customer bridge open for affected accounts. Holding on a full public incident post until we confirm hardware vs software.

kai (eng-runtime): Plan for follow-ups: 1) run targeted stress to reproduce KVCACHE OOM 2) test driver version rollback on canary 3) run hardware self-tests on quarantined nodes 4) long-term: guardrail to auto-fallback when KVCACHE memory pressure high.

jen (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline after 04:30 UTC. Maria, can you take primary for next 2 hours? I'll update rotation.

maria (sre): Taking over. I'll continue monitoring, coordinate vendor diagnostics, and prepare notes for post-incident.

jen (oncall): Thanks. Leaving in good shape — routing mitigations engaged, affected nodes cordoned, customer comms posted. :thumbsup:

incbot: Incident 3901234567 status: mitigated -> partial (customer-impact reduced). Next update scheduled in 30 minutes or on material change.

maria (sre): Uploading logs and preliminary timeline to incident artifacts now. Will file a follow-up bug for runtime KVCACHE protective limits.

raj (customer-ops): Sent customers update: "We mitigated transient errors by routing traffic and draining affected nodes. Investigations continue; we'll update within 30 minutes."

kai (eng-runtime): Quick note for postmortem: attach KVCACHE metrics (alloc/failures), driver reset traces, nv-host logs, and mapping of affected pod images. Also include replay test plan.

tom (support): Monitoring dashboards look stable; only isolated retries remain. Closing customer bridge in 1 hour if no regressions.

maria (sre): OK. I will start the post-incident checklist and flag for vendor hardware review if ECC corrected counts don't fall after one reboot.

incbot: Incident 3901234567 — last update recorded.
